Toy list of missing taxa, with allowed ranges

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges.Rd

Same as phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states, with biogeographic ranges as allowed states: the $allowed_states item holds ranges of phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges, coded as in BioGeoBEARS, in which each taxon can be grafted. It is used to showcase the grafting with biogeographic ranges as states, with treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE (see the Details section "Biogeographic ranges as states" of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()).

It is the output of phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() applied to the table system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_with_allowed_ranges.csv", package = "phylograftR"). Four taxa have a taxon-level value (one or several ranges) for $allowed_states and three have none (NULL), so they use the global allowed_states argument of the grafting function. All the allowed ranges are states of the toy simmap, so grafting does not raise warnings. Some are contained in other states of the simmap ("A" in "AB", "B" in "AB" and "BC"): a lineage grafted in a branch in "AB" with the allowed range "A" inherits "A", which is a subset sympatric speciation event, (AB) -> (AB), (A). Such a list requires a simmap to graft.

Usage

data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges)

Format

A named list with the same 7 taxa and items as phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list, and the extra item:

  • $allowed_states List (one element per taxon, named after the taxa) of character vectors of ranges of phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges in which the taxon can be grafted, or NULL to use the global allowed_states argument. "New_sp1": "A"; "New_sp4": "B" and "BC"; "New_sp5": "B"; "New_sp7": "A" and "BC"; the others: NULL.

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states for the same list, with allowed states of colors.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges for the stochastic character map of biogeographic ranges.

  • phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to import such a list from an external table.

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() to build such a list from a data.frame.

Examples

# Import the list
data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges)
toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges$allowed_states
#> $New_sp1
#> [1] "A"
#> 
#> $New_sp2
#> NULL
#> 
#> $New_sp3
#> NULL
#> 
#> $New_sp4
#> [1] "B"  "BC"
#> 
#> $New_sp5
#> [1] "B"
#> 
#> $New_sp6
#> NULL
#> 
#> $New_sp7
#> [1] "A"  "BC"
#> 

# Compare to the initial '.csv' file
system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_with_allowed_ranges.csv", package = "phylograftR")
#> [1] "/home/runner/.cache/R/renv/library/phylograftR-802cedf8/linux-ubuntu-resolute/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/phylograftR/extdata/toy_missing_taxa_with_allowed_ranges.csv"

# Graft with the toy simmap of ranges, treating the states as ranges
# Taxa with taxon-level ranges follow their specific constraints.
# Taxa without taxon-level ranges follow the global argument
# and can only be grafted on branches in a range containing "A" or "B".
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_simmap_ranges)

grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,
                                  missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges,
                                  simmap = toy_simmap_ranges, allowed_states = c("A", "B"),
                                  treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE,
                                  verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Plot the updated simmap
plot_grafted(grafted_phy,
             simmap_colors = c("A" = "gold", "B" = "dodgerblue",
                               "AB" = "limegreen", "BC" = "firebrick2"))


# Inspect range inherited by each grafted taxon (state of its terminal branch in the updated simmap)
taxon_names <- toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges$Taxon_name
tip_edges <- match(match(taxon_names, grafted_phy$tip.label), grafted_phy$edge[, 2])
taxon_ranges <- setNames(object = vapply(grafted_phy$simmap$maps[tip_edges],
                                         function (x) names(x)[1], character(1)),
                         nm = taxon_names)
# Should match with the allowed ranges. NULL default to "A" or "B"
# based on the 'allowed_ranges' argument.
taxon_ranges
#> New_sp1 New_sp2 New_sp3 New_sp4 New_sp5 New_sp6 New_sp7 
#>     "A"     "A"     "A"     "B"     "B"     "B"    "BC" 
toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges$allowed_states
#> $New_sp1
#> [1] "A"
#> 
#> $New_sp2
#> NULL
#> 
#> $New_sp3
#> NULL
#> 
#> $New_sp4
#> [1] "B"  "BC"
#> 
#> $New_sp5
#> [1] "B"
#> 
#> $New_sp6
#> NULL
#> 
#> $New_sp7
#> [1] "A"  "BC"
#>
